title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase: $4.56 (+5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $4.56 showed sales of 195 and 119 (x0.94 and x0.57 vs baseline). The deeper drop in 2026-10-05 suggests strong price sensitivity. No past promotion at this price. Noise-adjusted price effect is uncertain; shrink toward 1.0.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. A 5.1% price increase to $4.56 (from $4.34) is the only known driver. No past promotion at this price level exists. The 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 weeks saw sales of 195 and 119 at $4.56, both below baseline (207.6), indicating a price sensitivity effect. The noise-adjusted lift from past promotions (x1.36) is not applicable here as this is a price increase, not a discount. A price rise typically reduces demand; the 2026-10-05 week (x0.57) suggests a strong drop, but it may reflect a temporary dip or supply issue. Given the lack of a clear pattern and thin evidence, we shrink toward 1.0. The effect is uncertain, so we apply a small downside adjustment.

  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.2 - 290.7 | 10%-90%: 156.0 - 281.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
